title: eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y
summary: A public ESLint plugin that statically checks JSX for accessibility problems.
intended_users: JavaScript and React teams integrating accessibility feedback into lint workflows.

design_decisions.problem_or_constraint: Map JSX syntax and custom components to accessibility semantics without a running browser.
design_decisions.alternatives_considered: A monolithic rule is simpler but would weaken rule isolation, configuration, and targeted diagnostics.
design_decisions.chosen_approach_and_rationale: Separate rules, utilities, element-role data, configurations, and documentation behind ESLint's plugin interface.
design_decisions.accepted_trade_off: Static analysis cannot observe rendered behavior and depends on component mappings and rule configuration.
design_decisions.validation_approach: Review committed rule-valid and rule-invalid cases, utilities, configuration tests, and regressions without execution.
design_decisions.reconsideration_conditions: Revisit semantics and configuration boundaries as JSX frameworks and accessibility standards evolve.

testing_strategy: Committed rule and utility tests include valid, invalid, option, mapping, and regression cases; Finch never executes them.
security_threat: Security is not the selected track; do not infer security maturity from linting architecture.
production_limitation: Static evidence cannot verify lint execution, standards coverage, diagnostic accuracy, test success, or runtime accessibility.
technical_debt: Static checks must be combined with browser, assistive-technology, and human accessibility evaluation.
track_alignment_explanation: The plugin directly helps developers detect accessibility barriers in JSX.

ai_disclosure.purposes: No upstream AI-use claim; the calibration narrative was prepared without maintainer input.
ai_disclosure.review_validation: Human reference judgment froze before inference.
